newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Football League Tribunal cleared Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett of a striking charge last night, after hearing unwavering testimony protesting his innocence. The Tribunal took just eight minutes to find that Lockett had not struck Cllingwood's Scott Burns during the Swans win last Saturday at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Page 18.

Australian tennis player Jack Crawford, dubbed the founding father of the Grand Slam, was inducted into the Australian Tennis Hall of Fame yesterday. Crawford was the best player in the world in 1933, winning the Australian Open, Roland Garros and Wimbledon, but he lost in the United States missing out on what the New York Times dubbed the Grand Slam. Page 16.

The Canberra Raiders claimed their fifth successive Super League victory last night, defeating Auckland 20-10 in squalling conditions at Ericsson Stadium. The Raiders turn-around after a poor start to the season keeps them in the top five, while Auckland are at the bottom of the table. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

North Sydney Bears chairman Ray Beattie said yesterday Manly and North Sydney should consider merging with weaker clubs under a league compromise, rather than amalgamating with each other. Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker urged his board and the clubs not to be drawn on the subject. It is believed there is high-level support at North Sydney for a merger with Balmain or South Sydney if an amalgamation becomes necessary. Page 46.

New South Wales State of Origin coach Tom Raudonikis said last night his team may have to change tactics for tomorrow night's game against Queensland following an edict from the Australian Rugby League on violence, ruling that players who join or inflame situations will find themselves before the judiciary. Page 46

New Zealand officials have threatened to withhold the ACT Brumbies' profit share of the Super 12 final, due to a worsening of their dispute with the Australian Rugby Union. They are angry that the ACT has not paid Wellington their $96,750 share of gate-takings from their semi-final, and are currently seeking a review. Paying the fee would mean the ACT would only make about $50,000 from the semi-final played on their home ground. Page 46
THE AGE

The Australian men's basketball team, the Boomers, lost to Croatia by 19 points in Canberra last night, after trailing by 9 at half-time. It was the first time the Boomers have been defeated in the five-game international series. Page B6.

Australian hurdler Kyle Vander-Kuyp may disrupt his preparation for the world championships to return home to Australia for treatment to a hamstring injury sustained in his warm-up for the 110 metres hurdles at the Prefontaine Classic in Oregon last Sunday. He is being treated, but will consider returning to Australia if the injury does not respond quickly. Page B6.

West Coast Eagles player Chris Lewis was suspended for seven matches by the Australian Football League Tribunal last night after pleading guilty to two charges of striking against Essendon players on Sunday. Essendon's Danny Morgan and Barry Young had to be helped from the ground after sustaining head injuries from being struck by Lewis, who has apologised to both players. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Victoria has pulled back from a 0-3 deficit to win 4-3 over titleholders Woodlands in the Victorian Golf Association pennant final. Teenager Daniel Gaunt birdied the fifth play-off hole to clinch the victory, after rain had halted play. Page 65.

Joe Spiteri was prevented from training with the Socceroos in Melbourne yesterday after a preliminary scan revealed a possible stress fracture in his left foot. The Socceroos are in Melbourne as their first step towards the World Cup, and will play the first game of the Contenders series at Olympic Park tomorrow night. Page 69.

The Australian Football League's umpire's chief Bill Deller yesterday said the weekend's umpiring was the worst of the year, vowing to make changes to the panel for this weekend's round. The AFL said it would consider a suggestion that the best umpires officiate two games per round. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Jockey Club and the Sydney Turf Club have put their differences over the night racing issue on hold until their local councils have considered development proposals. Both are desperate to have night racing, but the New South Wales Government has stated it will only approve funding for one venue. Page 62.

Australian cricketer Glenn McGrath will escape without punishment after "giving the finger" to English fans at Lord's yesterday during Australia's third successive defeat in the Texaco Trophy one-day series against England. The incident was not reported by the umpires nor the match referee, and there was no reaction in the Australian camp. Page 62.

Australian women's golfer Karrie Webb finished third in a field of four players at the US LPGA Tour's Skins in Frisco yesterday, collecting $130,800. The tournament was a made-for-television event pitting the four dominant players on the women's tour against each other. Page 56.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
